what_it_does: This paper describes a high-resolution ADC (analog-to-digital converter) optimized for battery-powered sensors that need very low power consumption. High-resolution converters traditionally require power-hungry building blocks: delta-sigma modulators (circuits that use feedback and oversampling to achieve precision at the cost of energy) or zoom ADCs (which only work on DC signals). This design eliminates static (always-on) power by using dynamic comparators—transistors that only consume power when they're actively making a comparison—and dynamic reference generation. The key innovation is integrating noise-shaping (a technique to push quantization noise toward higher frequencies where it's easier to filter out) directly into the SAR (successive approximation register) ADC process itself, without needing the bulky feedback loops or precision amplifiers that traditional approaches require.
